OUR FANTASY FOOTBALL CUSTOM LEAGUE RULES

LAST UPDATED BY COMMISSIONER TIM ON 09.11.26

BELOW IS A FULL LIST OF OUR CUSTOM LEAGUE RULES, NOT INCLUDING RULES TRACKED WITHIN THE ESPN APP (SUCH AS ROSTER & SCORING SETTINGS).

Rule Changes:

  • All rule changes require a supermajority (>2/3rds) vote to pass. So 6 votes in an 8-person league or 7 votes in a 10-person league.

League Dues:

  • Currently $45/person, due via Venmo at the start of each year.

Winning Prizes:

  • The winner receives the following prizes:
  • Their name added to the trophy for perpetuity, and possession of the trophy until the next champion is crowned.
  • A championship ring of their choosing (with a display case).
  • One NFL jersey for the player of their choosing.
  • A banner celebrating their win.
  • Any remaining funds from the prize pot once all other prizes have been disbursed.
  • Starting with the 2026 Season, $45 of the league dues is deposited in the League Trust (previously, second place would get their dues back)

Last Place Punishment:

  • Whoever finishes the season in last place must serve as the MAID at the following season’s draft, where they must wear some sort of costume and serve drinks to the rest of the league. Amendments to this rule include:
  • The implementation of a MAID BELL, effective in the 2025 season.
  • The implementation of a MAID CHUG to begin the draft.
  • The winner of the maid bowl the previous season will walk the maid down the stairs to introduce them at the start of the draft.
  • If the maid is unable to fulfill their maid duties at the following year’s draft, they may do one of the following options:
  • Someone may volunteer to serve as maid on their behalf.
  • They may postpone their duties to the following year’s draft; HOWEVER, if they finish in last place again, or they miss a consecutive draft year as maid, they then become SUPERMAID (the duties of which will be determined by the rest of the league if and when a supermaid comes to pass).

Playoffs:

  • We have a custom play-in system:
  • Week 15: Play-in
  • 1 vs. 2  - matchup to determine top seed for playoffs
  • 3 vs. 4 vs. 5 vs. 6 - one week group play -- 2 teams with the highest points in that week advance to playoffs
  • 7 vs. 8 vs. 9 vs. 10 - one week group play -- Seeding for consolation bracket (eg. highest points get 7 seed, lowest points gets 10 seed)
  • Week 16: Semifinals
  • 1 seed vs. 3 or 4 seed (their choice)
  • 2 seed vs. remaining 3/4 seed
  • Play-in loser #1 (5 seed) vs. Play-in loser #2 (6 seed)
  • 7 seed vs. 10 seed
  • 8 seed vs. 9 seed
  • Week 17: Finals
  • 1v4 winner vs. 2v3 winner: Championship
  • 1v4 loser vs. 2v3 loser: Winner chooses next year’s draft location 
  • 5v6 winner vs. highest-seeded winner of previous round (so 7 seed if they won, or winner of 8v9 if 7 lost): winner gets #1 Draft Pick
  • 5v6 loser vs. lower-seeded winner of previous round (10 seed if they won, or winner of 8v9): winner gets #3 Draft Pick
  • 7v10 loser vs. 8v9 loser: loser becomes maid

On Draft:

  • Prior to the draft, the league will get the opportunity to choose their draft spot. The order in which people get to choose a spot is based on the previous year’s final standings:
  • 5th place (first person out of the playoffs): #1 choice
  • 6th place: #2
  • 7th place: #3
  • 8th place: #4
  • 9th place: #5
  • 10th place: #6
  • 4th place: #7
  • 3rd place: #8
  • 2nd place: #9
  • 1st place: #10

Tanking Rules:

  • Anyone who intentionally leaves an active roster spot empty or starts a player who is not playing will be subject to the punishment of being moved to last place in the following week’s waiver order.
  • It is sometimes difficult to establish intent, but here are some examples of what is not considered intentional:
  • Being unable to field a full roster due to bye weeks/injuries: unintentional.
  • Having a player ruled out at the last minute and not putting in a replacement in time: unintentional.
  • Due to the frequency of players not fielding a full roster, the responsibility of determining intent will usually fall to the commissioner to determine if a team meets the criteria to be punished for intentional tanking (and such punishment, if enforced, will be announced in the chat). HOWEVER, if the commissioner’s decision in this matter is questioned by anyone in the league it will be put to a simple-majority league vote (6 votes needed to pass in a 10 team league) which overrules the decision of the commissioner.

Miscellaneous Rules:

  • If for some reason a manager is unable to adjust their lineup in the Fantasy app (i.e., they’re in an area with bad service), they can message the commissioner to make the change for them as long as the request comes through prior to kickoff.
  • In extreme events like COVID where players are at risk of being ruled out after lineups have been locked, players can also make requests in advance for alternate players to be subbed in if their original choice does not play. These decisions must be made prior to the kickoff of all games involved and are considered final once the game has started.
  • PROP 2: Anybody who leaves the Fantasy Football Messenger group chat is not allowed to make a trade until they have returned to the chat for at least 24 hours.
  • AMENDMENT TO PROP 2: Whenever somebody leaves the Facebook Messenger chat during the season, they cannot be readded until they submit an apology video (minimum 30 seconds) where they explain and apologize for their actions.
  • THE LEAGUE TRUST: A percentage of league dues are put into a high yield savings account or stock portfolio and in 10 years we take the trust and blow it on that years draft. Allocation of funds are voted on and a yearly financial report is presented at draft or owners meeting.
  • RECORD-BREAKING FIELD GOALS ARE WORTH 15 POINTS: If a team is starting a kicker who breaks the record for longest NFL field goal (currently 68 yards going into the 2026 season), that field goal will be worth 15 points (right now such a field goal would be worth 5 points; the commissioner would manually add another 10 points to that player's score). The field goal must break the record, not tie it -- the first kick to receive this bonus must be recorded as at least 69 yards.

FOR ANY CONTROVERSIAL MATTERS NOT COVERED ABOVE:

  • Short-term conflicts such as accusations of collusion, matchup controversies, or basically anything that happens within a season shall be put to a simple-majority vote (as opposed to the supermajority two-thirds vote that is reserved for making changes to the long-term future of the league).
  • If the vote results in a tie, the commissioner holds the tiebreaker UNLESS the controversial matter directly involves the commissioner, in which case the commissioner will be recused from the vote.
